title: Bigger paychecks take center stage in Trump’s economic push
summary: Fox Business panel on Trump's boom-year pitch: tariffs bring in billions with no inflation, Forbes says prices still feel high, Dagen argues tariffs are a one-time price hit and slowing growth explains cooler inflation.

assertions.quote: BECAUSE OF TARIFFS WE ARE TAKING AND BILLIONS OF DOLLARS MORE THAN WE EVER HAD BEFORE. WITH NO INFLATION BY THE WAY, NO INFLATION.
PRACTICALLY NO INFLATION AND WE ARE TAKING IN HUNDREDS OF BILLIONS OF DOLLARS.

verdicts.note: CPI rose about 2.7% over 2025; low by recent standards but not zero.
The 12-month CPI-U change ran between 2.3% and 3.0% in every month of 2025, and the index rose 2.0% from January to December 2025.

assertions.quote: WHEN YOU GO TO THE SUPERMARKET A LOT OF THINGS ARE STILL GOING UP. PRICES ARE STILL HIGH IN A LOT OF AREAS.

verdicts.note: Price levels stay elevated after a disinflation; food at home and shelter were both still rising in late 2025.

By December 2025 the shelter index was 420.134, 28% above December 2020 (327.702) and still rising 3.2% a year, and the food index was 343.795, 27% above December 2020 (270.023), while headline inflation had fallen to 2.7%; falling inflation left price levels elevated.

assertions.quote: THE SUPREME COURT WILL RULE AGAINST HIM ON TARIFFS AND THAT WILL BE GOOD FOR THE ECONOMY

verdicts.note: Most models find the 2025 tariffs a net drag on output and real incomes, so removing them raises GDP modestly.

assertions.quote: I NEVER THOUGHT THE TARIFFS WERE INFLATIONARY. THEY ARE A SLIVER OF A VALUE-ADDED TAX SOURCE CONSUMPTION TAX. IT'S ALREADY BAKED IN.

verdicts.note: The tariff effect on the consumer goods price level peaked near 3 percent in February 2026 and stays positive, while the contribution to twelve-month goods inflation peaked at 2.9 points, falls to about zero by August 2026 and then turns negative as the 2025 increases drop out of the comparison.

Business surveys show firms spreading tariff-related price increases over extended periods, so what is in principle a one-time price-level adjustment is in practice drawn out, especially when tariffs change frequently.

assertions.quote: ONE REASON INFLATION MIGHT BE COMING DOWN IS BECAUSE THE UNEMPLOYMENT RATE IS AT 4.6%, SAME FOR OIL.

verdicts.note: Unemployment drifted up to about 4.6% and oil fell in 2025, both disinflationary, alongside the fading of the 2021-22 shock.

assertions.quote: WE BROUGHT IN ABOUT $200 BILLION IN TARIFF REVENUE FOR THE FULL FISCAL YEAR. SO THAT COVERS TOO -- TWO MONTHS ON INTEREST

verdicts.note: Tariffs raised roughly $200-300 billion a year against about $1.2 trillion of interest and a near-$2 trillion deficit.

assertions.quote: CURRENT CONDITIONS SLIDE TO A RECORD LOW.

verdicts.note: The University of Michigan current-conditions index set a record low in December 2025 even as expectations improved.
